To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The Highway network is an architecture that can be used to train very deep networks.

(1) the training and testing errors of a deep network are not monotonically decreasing with the depth of a network, (2) the training and test errors are nonmonotonic in the depth, and (3) there are optimal values of depth for both the training and test error, and the optimal depth is different for different datasets.
1. The Highway and Residual Networks are capable of learning unrolled iterative estimation algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of depth in learning architectures and the design of deep learning algorithms for large scale learning tasks.
the development of new deep learning architectures that are able to learn unrolled iterative estimation algorithms.
the design of new architectures and algorithms for training very deep neural networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residual learning framework can be viewed as a form of regularization that can dramatically ease the training of networks that contain very deep layers.
the ResNet model is the most powerful and efficient model for image classification.
the residual network has a better accuracy than the highway network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we showed how to train deep networks by unrolling the optimization algorithm and using it as an iterative estimation algorithm.
the new architectures are able to learn unrolled iterations of iterative estimation methods such as fixed-point iterations, Newton’s method, and gradient descent.
these networks are able to learn iterative optimization algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the success of these networks can be explained in terms of unrolled iterative estimation, a simple and intuitive principle that has been used in the past to explain the success of other iterative algorithms, such as the EM algorithm.
the key to training these networks is to unroll the iterative estimation process they perform.
these new architectures are not only a clever way of making gradient descent more effective but also a way of learning unrolled iterative estimation algorithms.
